title: Disorder-driven transport in ZrN thin films grown by ion-beam-assisted sputtering
authors: Maximo DiPreta, Samuel Jiang, Serhii Kruhlov, Yi Li, Valentine Novosad, Tomas Polakovic
abstract: We investigate the structural and electronic transport properties of zirconium nitride (ZrN) thin films grown by dc ion-beam assisted sputtering (IBAS) as a function of nitrogen partial pressure, sputtering power and deposition temperature. Variation of growth conditions enables controlled tuning from disordered metallic and superconducting behavior to insulating transport. Increasing nitrogen flow drives an increase in sheet resistance, suppression of superconducting transition temperature, and non-metallic conduction. XRD shows no measurable change in long range crystallinity or order. In the insulating regime, low-temperature transport is well described by 3D Mott variable-range hopping (VRH), with the characteristic temperature $T_0$ increasing monotonically with sheet resistance over four orders of magnitude. Despite this strong correlation between $T_0$ and disorder, $T_c$ exhibits no systematic dependence on $T_0$, indicating a decoupling between localization physics and the superconducting energy scale. Magnetotransport measurements are not well described by the standard BCS model nor the dirty type-II Werthamer-Helfand-Hohenberg model. The phase boundary is instead captured by a free-exponent power law, $μ_0 H_{c2}(T) = μ_0 H_{c2}(0)[1 - (T/T_c)^{n}]$ with $n \approx 3.47$, and extrapolates to $μ_0 H_{c2}(0) \approx 6.4$ T. The films have an extracted coherence length of 7 nm. These results establish IBAS-grown ZrN as a broadly tunable platform for investigating disorder-driven transport and the crossover between metallic conduction, electronic localization, and superconductivity.
summary: This work establishes ZrN thin films grown by IBAS as a highly tunable platform to study the interplay between disorder, localization, and superconductivity. By controlling growth parameters, the researchers tune the material through metallic, insulating (Mott VRH), and superconducting regimes. The key finding is the decoupling between the localization scale and the superconducting critical temperature, offering insights into the nature of pairing in disordered superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates disorder-driven transport and the crossover between metallic conduction, electronic localization, and superconductivity in ZrN thin films.
main_result: The system exhibits a clear decoupling between the superconducting energy scale ($T_c$) and the localization physics (Mott VRH scale $T_0$), suggesting distinct physical origins for these phenomena.
method: The research combines controlled thin-film synthesis via ion-beam-assisted sputtering (IBAS) with comprehensive electrical transport measurements, including low-temperature resistivity and magnetotransport.
model_or_system: The physical system is ZrN thin films grown by IBAS, allowing tuning of disorder by varying nitrogen partial pressure and deposition temperature. The analysis models transport using 3D Mott Variable-Range Hopping (VRH) for localization and fits the upper critical field ($H_{c2}(T)$) to an empirical power law.
key_observables: Sheet resistance ($R_\square$), superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), Mott characteristic temperature ($T_0$), and the upper critical field ($\mu_0 H_{c2}(T)$).
important_parameters: Nitrogen partial pressure, sputtering power, deposition temperature, coherence length ($\xi(0) \approx 7	ext{ nm}$), and the exponent $n \approx 3.47$ for the $H_{c2}(T)$ fit.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that superconductivity develops within individual crystalline columns, while the insulating behavior (VRH) is governed by transport across inter-columnar boundaries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of resistance and $T_c$ with growth conditions, show the linear relationship between $\ln R$ and $T^{-1/4}$ confirming VRH, and plot the magnetic field dependence of $H_{c2}(T)$ against various theoretical models.
paper_structure: The paper systematically explores the effect of growth parameters on microstructure and transport, first establishing the tunable nature of the material, then analyzing the insulating regime via VRH, and finally characterizing the superconducting phase boundary.
why_interesting: The clear separation of the disorder-induced localization scale ($T_0$) from the superconducting scale ($T_c$) provides a clean experimental platform to study how disorder affects different quantum phenomena independently.
